questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I visited New Zealand some years ago and fell in love with Oceania. However, I did not visit Australia, even though I really wanted to. As a result I agreed with myself on going on an exchange in Australia instead in the future, which is why I went in the fall of 2024.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was the greatest experience of my life so fare.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I revived a lot of information before I arrived, such as the opportunity to book a free transfer to my accommodation, which company provided the best reception etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult. The housing market in Melbourne is awful, and it’s very difficult to find something affordable even for Copenhagen standards.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It’s almost impossible to find off campus housing before you arrive. So if you have the opportunity I would recommend arriving in Melbourne 2 or 3 weeks time before school starts in order to find a place to live. Another possibility is to ask is Facebook groups made for Danish people in Melbourne. It was my impression that some students found acclimation through Facebook pages like that or groups like “fairy floss”.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing available for student through Monash was primarily placed out side the city which isn’t optimal for exchange students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Difficult

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Calling or writing regarding my questions or looking on the website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look in to the process in advance! It takes time!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was okay, however a bit lower than what I’m used to at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. My courses were all intensive courses, hence they took place over a few weeks each and then classes were done. This approach is very different from what I have experienced at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Since I was studying at the city campus there didn’t seem to be that many opportunities at the campus. I think these activities were located at the campus in Clayton and Canfield. However, I didn’t really research it, so I might be wrong.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of clubs and social gatherings.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don’t know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The national parks in Victoria, including The Grampian, Otway Rainforrest etc. Also go visit Tasmania. The place is fantastic!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of Chinese students and students from other countries in Asia which did also attend the University. I encountered more “difficulties” with these student compared to the local ones, as their culture is so different from mine. However, they were very friendly and talkative.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The coffee culture, the food scene and much more!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- The postgraduate law faculty is placed in the centre of the city NOT in Clayton or Caulfield.
- Housing is expensive in Melbourne.
- The postgraduate law courses are so called “intensive” courses which runs over a few weeks in stead of the whole semester.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything! I cannot choose only one thing. However, Melbourne is amazing!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting use to studying, reading and writing in English exclusively.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
